stemMd: According to Table 4, as the water temperature increased from $10\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $70\;^{\circ}\text{C}$, the mass of Salt R that dissolved in $100.0$ g of water:
explanationMd:
Read down the Salt R column from the top row to the bottom row, in order of increasing temperature:

- $10\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $12.6$ g
- $25\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $10.9$ g
- $40\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $9.4$ g
- $55\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $8.1$ g
- $70\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $7.0$ g

Every value is smaller than the one above it, so the mass falls at every step and never rises. The trend is a decrease only.

Check it by taking the differences between neighbouring rows: $-1.7$, $-1.5$, $-1.3$, $-1.1$. All four differences are negative, which confirms that there is no point at which the column turns around. A useful habit on a trend question is to compute those step-by-step differences rather than just comparing the first and last values — comparing only the ends would give the same answer here, but it would miss a column that rose in the middle before falling back.

distractorRationale.a: This is the trend shown by Salt P and Salt Q, not Salt R. A reader who takes hold of the wrong column, or who assumes that heating water must always let more solid dissolve, picks this.
distractorRationale.b: This describes a column that rises to a peak and then falls. No such turning point appears in the Salt R column; every one of its four step-by-step differences is negative.
distractorRationale.c: Salt Q changes by less than $2$ g across the whole range and could loosely be called almost unchanged, but Salt R changes from $12.6$ g to $7.0$ g, a drop of $5.6$ g — a $44\%$ fall that is far too large to call no change.

accessibilityText: The question uses the Salt R column of Table 4, which gives the mass in grams dissolving in 100.0 grams of water at five temperatures. At 10 degrees Celsius, 12.6 grams; at 25 degrees, 10.9 grams; at 40 degrees, 9.4 grams; at 55 degrees, 8.1 grams; at 70 degrees, 7.0 grams.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Salt R values in order are 12.6, 10.9, 9.4, 8.1 and 7.0 g. Each is lower than the one before, so the mass decreased only.

review.notes: Author solved the item and then tried to defend each distractor. The Salt R column falls at every one of its four steps, so 'decreased only' is the only defensible description: 'increased only' and 'increased then decreased' are contradicted by the sign of every difference, and 'remained the same' is contradicted by a 5.6 g change. Exactly one option survives. Awaiting an independent blind solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
